730000102.text: #Don't be afraid, we're not bad Nara! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. You're Ararycan, right?

730000104.text: That's right! Araja sent us here, saying that you could help us.

730000107.text: Wah... there's been strange Nara around, that's why I was a bit scared.

730000108.text: We didn't mean to scare you! It's just that we didn't know you were so absorbed in...

730000109.text: Mmm... Since you can see Ararycan and are friends with Araja, the forest must recognize you. You can't be bad Nara.

730000110.text: Mm-hmm. You are good Nara. Ararycan is not afraid. Did you say that you have questions for Ararycan?

730000106.text: That's right! We've got some questions.

730000201.text: Ah! How did you get up here?

730000202.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, that's the suspicious Nara. He's been sneaking around here with that suspicious machine.

730000203.text: Mmm, you're right. Coming to a place like this is pretty suspicious, alright...

730000204.text: Um, I'd say you're the suspicious ones here. After all, I am a certified researcher from the Akademiya, and you are outlanders of unknown origin.

730000209.text: Oh, a commission? So you're adventurers. Or perhaps you're Eremites or something?

730000210.text: Well, it doesn't matter. My name is Jazari, a Kshahrewar Researcher, as you can see. I don't care what you came here for, but don't get in the way of my research.

730000211.text: What's there to be researched in this deep cave?

730000212.text: There are always things to be researched everywhere. As the saying goes, "ignorance is a researcher's disgrace."

730000213.text: You must have noticed the huge ruin machine out there, right? That is actually a Ruin Golem made in the ancient realm of Khaenri'ah.

730000214.text: In the local lexicon of Khaenri'ah, the name might possibly have been something like "Mechanical Warden."

730000215.text: See? We're right behind the Ruin Golem. The machine's operator, should there have been one, would have entered from here.

730000216.text: Hmm... But a machine of this size would have required more than one operator, right?

730000217.text: Aha, that's among my research topics! Unfortunately, I haven't made much progress so far.

730000218.text: Exploring the Ruin Golem from the inside seems to be the only solution, and I am presently looking for a way in.

730000219.text: You sound more suspicious by the minute...

730000220.text: #That's right, we did meet an Abyss Order member disguised as a researcher that one time! Paimon reckons he was called Enjou... {NICKNAME}, do you remember what happened to him again?

730000221.text: We beat the snot out of him.

730000222.text: Hey, hey! Please don't! I'm a legitimate researcher...

730000223.text: Ugh, you don't believe me, do you... See this? This is an Investigation Charter from the Akademiya, with the highest possible level of clearance.

730000224.text: That's not something to be given away on the streets. Certainly not one concerning investigations into ancient ruins as important as this. The Akademiya would never issue something like this casually.

730000225.text: I can't give you the original copy, but... Wait a second, where did I put my Kamera... I remember placing it inside my bag...

730000226.text: Be careful! He's taking that suspicious machine out again.

730000227.text: Jazari sets the device up carefully.\nIt is indeed a Kamera.

730000228.text: Eh? Is this the suspicious machine you mentioned? It's just a Kamera...

730000230.text: That's right. It's a machine that takes pictures. It's pretty convenient!

730000231.text: Yes. This is a priceless item as far as the Akademiya is concerned. I can't just let you touch it... Wait. Who were you talking to just now?

730000208.text: Ahem! We've been commissioned to investigate the situation here.

730000401.text: Some fate must have dictated that we would meet here. But that friend of yours... *sigh*

730000402.text: She must have led a lonely life. Be nice to her.

730000403.text: Anyway, I have to organize my findings. So, if you would excuse me...

730001601.text: Heh, finally believe me, do you?

730001602.text: Yep, guess you're not suspicious after all, Jazari.

730001603.text: We have some questions about the situation...

730001604.text: Hehe, ask away. As a Kshahrewar researcher who specializes in studying ruin machines, I've been investigating this big guy over here for years.

730001605.text: No one on this earth knows more about this Ruin Golem than I do.

730001606.text: What about beneath the earth, then?

730001608.text: Legends hold that the ancient realm of Khaenri'ah lies beneath the earth. Since they built all the ruin machines, it would be arrogant of me to say that I understand these devices better than they do.

730001609.text: Tell me about the "bad dirty stuff"...

730001610.text: Haha, you're looking for bad and dirty things, are you? Then you should visit the city.

730001611.text: The city? Are bad things in the city?

730001615.text: Anyway, this locale is somewhat polluted, which might be related to the "bad and dirty stuff" you mentioned.

730001616.text: Well, here's the situation. We've heard that the forest here has...

730001617.text: You paraphrase Ararycan's words so that Jazari can understand them...

730001618.text: Is that so? Let me think about this... I might indeed have some clues.

730001619.text: According to my research, all ruin mechanisms work on the same principle no matter what they do, whether it be flying or launching missiles...

730001620.text: And well, a Ruin Golem is theoretically the same as a Ruin Guard, except that it was to be operated by people. Have you noticed anything abnormal about this Ruin Golem?

730000501.text: Paimon needs friends? Ararycan could be your friend.

730000503.text: Um... Thanks, you two, but that's not the problem!

730000504.text: The issue is that he can't see you, Ararycan.

730000505.text: Mm-hmm. When Nara grow up, they can't really see Aranara anymore. Young Nara see us because they are innocent. But grown Nara can't.

730000506.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is a dreamer, favored by trees and flowers, so you can still see us, even as a grown-up.

730000507.text: Anyway, we should be more careful when talking to Aranara in front of others...

730000508.text: Well, Paimon doesn't think Jazari was lying, anyway. You might have misunderstood him, Ararycan.

730000509.text: Ararycan saw that Nara taking out his... Kamera, and doing *ka-chick* to hilinara. Very suspicious.

730000510.text: If that Nara isn't bad... Ah, he runs away every time the hilinara come. So he can't really be friends with the hilinara.

730000513.text: Mm-hmm, the Nara holds his machine and runs so fast.

730000514.text: So he shouldn't be a bad person. Nor should he be related to the children at Vimara Village...

730001101.text: This price... Did you come all the way here to make fun of me?

730000801.text: Well, you have a deal! I mean, Mora does come after friendship for us dealers, so I'll do you three a friendly favor today. There, I'll sell you the antique at the price you've named.

730001303.text: Isn't this just a normal Chaos Core!?

730001304.text: Nonsense. That's no ordinary Chaos Core, but the core of a Ruin Guard prototype found in Stormterror's Lair.

730001305.text: See the marks left by the Great Wolf King of the North? This is a unique treasure alright, and no mistake!

730001306.text: Eh? Then isn't this the one we saw at Stormterror's Lair? Didn't Dain take it?

730001307.text: This one's got to be a fake!

730001309.text: Whoa, that's impressive understanding for someone your age.

730001310.text: Wait, but that's not the point!

730001312.text: Well, I don't know about this Dain fellow, but I sure have heard of Stormterror's Lair. Anyway, if you have different insights about antiques, we could discuss them in private...

730001313.text: Whatever this is, it's definitely not the Amiti Device.

730001314.text: What I'm looking for is a key that can open up the Ruin Golem on Devantaka Mountain.

730001315.text: According to my research, it should be in the hands of your grandfather, Mr. Hasad, the Golden Adventurer.

730001316.text: Well, at least that was the case several decades ago...

730001317.text: Jazari describes the story of Mr. Hasad the Golden Adventurer as recorded in documents.

730001318.text: Oh, come on. You should have just said this earlier.

730001320.text: Haha, but that really brings back memories. It's been so long since I last heard stories about my grandpa.

730001321.text: When I was little, grandpa would often tell me stories of his adventures. I thought then that he was just bragging, but what do you know, he actually was that awesome.

730001322.text: Speaking of which, it is mostly because of him that I became an appraiser of antiques. All the stories about treasures were just so intriguing.

730001323.text: Still, the thing you spoke of is not here with me.

730001324.text: Eh? You haven't sold it off, have you?

730001325.text: I wish I did... But treasures don't stay where they don't belong, as they say. I mean, isn't that what happens in all treasure-hunting legends?

730001326.text: Well, Grandpa didn't care about any of that stuff, but according to him, that device engraved with ancient characters was lost during one of his adventures in some underground cave.

730001327.text: That was a long story, one which he told me so many times. But... I can't remember a single word of it now.

730001328.text: Actually, I even planned a treasure hunt for it with some others back then. And as to whether we really found it again... Well, if we did, it should still be hidden in a secret base at Vimara Village.

730001420.text: Haha, I always went there to play when I was just a kid. You know how kids love their secret bases.

730001421.text: Could you please show us to the secret base? Perhaps we could find some clues there.

730001422.text: So this thing is that important to you, huh? Still, I haven't been back for many years...

730001202.text: I see how it is. You're not buying anything, are you? I didn't do decades of business here just to be messed with!

730001203.text: No, no, that's not what we meant...

730001205.text: Hmm... What are we gonna do, Jazari?

730001206.text: *sob* I'll have to accept that for the sake of my research...

730000701.text: Welcome. You must be travelers from abroad. What brings you here to my shop? Would you like to make any purchases or seek to appraise any items?

730000702.text: So you're Royinjan, the antique dealer, right?

730000703.text: Royinjan, the Chief Antique Appraiser, to be precise. Did you come specifically to visit me? Well, I shan't let you down then.

730000704.text: We're looking for a certain antique.

730000705.text: Oh? Then you've come to the right place. If you can name it, Royinjan here can tell you about it.

730000706.text: I've probably seen enough antiques to lay out across the entire marketplace. Even the Akademiya might not have seen quite as many.

730000707.text: We're looking for the... Um, what's the thingy's name again? Paimon can't remember.

730000708.text: Hi, we're looking for an Amiti Device.

730000709.text: Eh? I've never heard of something like that.

730000710.text: Hey! You just said that we could name anything!

730000711.text: Haha, don't worry. I haven't heard of that name, but I might yet know of the thing you want. Antiques tend to have a variety of monikers, you see.

730000712.text: Can you describe the thing that you're looking for?

730000713.text: Ugh, how should I put it? The documents didn't include a particularly detailed description...

730000714.text: It's an item in the style of those ruin machines, and it should be an identification device of sorts.

730000715.text: It should be marked with unique Khaenri'ah-style patterns, that can be recognized to be chronologically different from the common types seen on Ruin Guards, thus marking this as some sort of earlier version of the device...

730000716.text: And considering what we know of ruin archaeology...

730000717.text: Ah, alright, you can stop now. I know what you're looking for.

730000718.text: Ha, so you know? That's so very helpful, thank you. In that case, please give it to me.

730000719.text: Uh, that's not how this works. This item is very precious. If you really want it, you'll have to pay for it. And that's... 500,000 Mora, at the very least.

730000721.text: It's an antique, you know. What I'm offering is a pretty common price.

730000722.text: Ugh... But what if the Mora we spend here can't guarantee a successful report...

730000723.text: #Let's just help him out, shall we, {NICKNAME}?

730000724.text: We've helped others bargain before, haven't we? You're probably a dab hand by now.

730000727.text: Really? That's... a relief. I'm terrible at things like this.

730000728.text: That's everything on me. Just take it. I'll have to find a gig with the Eremite over there if that's not sufficient, though.

730000901.text: *sigh* Fine, I'll just make do with that amount. But treat the item well, okay? Each antique has many stories and emotions behind it.

730001001.text: Hmm, this price is a little too low... You know what I mean?

730009901.text: Hey, that must be the "Ararycan" who was mentioned earlier, right? Let's go ask him!
